archetype: Melee STR warrior rebuilt around a two-stance kit. Shinsoku skills are the fast, low-commitment half of the kit; Battou skills are the slow, heavy half. Using a Battou skill puts the character into the Akatsuki state, which grants final damage and ignore-defense for its duration, so the intended loop alternates between the two stances to hold Akatsuki up rather than committing to one stance. The 5th job buff Shogetsu Form layers on top of that state with higher multipliers, knockback immunity and amplified Battou damage. IMPORTANT: this describes the REWORKED Hayato introduced in GMS v266 (The Sengoku Warrior Reawakening). The pre-v266 kit (Rai Sanrenzan, Hitokiri Strike, Jin Battoujutsu) no longer exists and most guides still on the open web describe it.

gearingNotes:
CLASS-SPECIFIC HOOKS, all from the current post-revamp source unless noted.

1. The link skill is CONDITIONAL and the condition is a gearing target. Moonlit Blade Learnings only pays out at 100%+ Critical Rate and 50% Critical Damage. Both the link skill and the Legion effect give Critical Damage, so the class's own contributions push one side of a threshold that requires the other side to be satisfied first from gear and hyper stats.

2. The class supplies a large amount of crit from passives - roughly +45% Critical Rate and +30% Critical Damage base from its own skills (rising into the 65-67% range on Critical Damage with buffs). That materially changes where crit investment stops paying off compared to a class with no passive crit, and it is the reason a flat cross-class hyper stat or inner ability recommendation is a poor fit here.

3. Ignore DEF is around +48% from passives, reaching roughly +72.7% with buffs active. IED stacks multiplicatively, so a high passive baseline lowers the marginal value of further IED from gear and hyper stats.

4. Attack speed reaches 8 from passives, with a 1.25x weapon multiplier and 99% weapon mastery. Because the class is already fast natively, the +1 attack speed inner ability line is not among either source's recommended lines.

5. Akatsuki uptime is the mechanical constraint that gear should serve. Because Akatsuki is entered by using a Battou skill and grants final damage plus ignore-defense for its duration, buff duration has more value here than it would for a class with no maintained state - which is consistent with Buff Duration +38% appearing as a recommended inner ability line.

STALE, FROM THE v252 DOC AND FLAGGED AS SUCH - recorded only so they are not mistaken for current advice: a 10 attack speed target via Booster / Quick Draw / green potions / Decent Speed Infusion, a 95-97% visual IED target, Princess No's Kodachi as the secondary, Attack-line WSE with 9 attack preferred, and a cooldown hat as optional quality-of-life. The secondary weapon choice and WSE advice are the most likely of these to have survived the rework, but none of it was confirmed against a post-v266 source.
commonMistakes: Using any Hayato guide that names Rai Sanrenzan, Rai Blade Flash, Hitokiri Strike or Jin Battoujutsu: Owari No Susanoo. Those skills belong to the pre-v266 class and no longer exist. This is the dominant failure mode for Hayato specifically, because the class doc linked from both the community wiki index and from Grandis Library is one of those guides.

Treating the linked class doc 'The Way of the Blade' as current. It is the top result a player will find, it is the doc the ecosystem points at, and it is stranded at v252 - before the v266 Sengoku Warrior Reawakening. Its 6th job section in particular describes an Origin skill the class does not have.

Counting Grandis Library and the Hayato class doc as two agreeing sources. Grandis credits the Hayato Discord for its inner ability, hyper passive and boost node fields, and the doc comes from that same Discord. They are one consensus family.
Rolling attack speed on inner ability. The class already reaches attack speed 8 from passives and no source recommends the line.

Assuming the link skill is working. Moonlit Blade Learnings does nothing until the character is at 100%+ Critical Rate and 50% Critical Damage, so on a fresh or low-progression character it can be contributing zero while appearing active.

Trusting a node-trio table's date stamp. The one consolidated cross-class trio reference used here displays 'Last update: November 21st, 2024' while simultaneously listing post-v266 skill names for both Hayato and Kanna - its own date line is demonstrably wrong, in the direction of understating currency.

sources.what: Hayato class Discord. Credited by Grandis Library as the source of its inner ability, hyper passive and boost node judgement, and the destination MapleDoro redirects to for HEXA. Given that the public class doc is stranded pre-revamp, this is almost certainly the only live source of post-v266 Hayato HEXA investment order. Not machine-readable - requires a human to join and read pins.

conflicts.topic: Boost node trio composition - which Moon Cut belongs in the main trio
conflicts.positionA: Trio #1 is [Shinsoku] Mist Slash + [Shinsoku] Crescent Moon Cut + [Shinsoku] Afterimage Slash, with [Battou] Full Moon's Rage and [Shinsoku] Silent Arc forming a second, two-skill trio.
conflicts.positionB: The first trinode is [Shinsoku] Mist Slash + [Battou] Full Moon's Rage + either [Shinsoku] Crescent Moon Cut or [Battou] Dark Moon Cut, and the second is [Shinsoku] Silent Arc + [Shinsoku] Afterimage Slash + either [Shinsoku] Grazing Cut or [Shinsoku] Stormcloud Splitter.
conflicts.status: contested - recorded, not resolved. Both positions re-read verbatim 2026-09-12; the disagreement is real and not an extraction artifact. The two sources place Full Moon's Rage and Afterimage Slash in different trios. Neither is strong enough to override the other: one has a demonstrably wrong date stamp, the other is a content farm. Resolve via the Hayato Discord.

conflicts.topic: Which skills are boostable at all
conflicts.positionA: The boost node table lists six nodes covering Mist Slash, Grazing Cut + Reactive Focus, Dark Moon Cut, Afterimage Slash, Full Moon's Rage, and Silent Arc. Crescent Moon Cut and Stormcloud Splitter do not appear.
conflicts.positionB: Crescent Moon Cut and Stormcloud Splitter are named as trio members, implying they are boostable.
conflicts.status: contested - most likely a collapsed-content truncation on the first source rather than a real disagreement, since that page carries a 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' toggle. Node membership was identical across four reads of the Grandis table, so the truncation, if that is what it is, is consistent. Flagged so the six-node list is not treated as exhaustive.

conflicts.topic: Boost node tier ordering (PRIMARY / SECONDARY / OTHER)
conflicts.positionA: FOUR separate reads of the same source page returned FOUR different tier assignments. The skill contents of each node were identical across all four reads; only the labels moved.
conflicts.positionB: No second source publishes a Hayato boost node tier ordering at all - confirmed 2026-09-12 against DigitalTQ, mastermysty and MapleDoro.
conflicts.status: unresolved - a reading-reliability conflict, not a disagreement between guides. Deliberately left blank in vMatrix.priority rather than resolved by majority reading.

conflicts.topic: What Twilight Bloom and Princess Sakuno's Blessing ARE - cross-class Sengoku nodes, or Hayato's own 5th job skills
conflicts.positionA: Both are things every Sengoku class should also pick up, framed as shared rather than class-specific: 'All Sengoku classes should try to also obtain these: Twilight Bloom, Princess Sakuno's Blessing.'
conflicts.positionB: Both are listed among Hayato's OWN 5th job skills, alongside Shogetsu Form, Weapon Aura, Impenetrable Skin and [Battou] Wailing Heavens.
conflicts.status: contested - RECORDED 2026-09-12, previously missing from this file. Both readings were re-verified verbatim on that date. This is a classification disagreement, not a factual one about whether the skills exist - they exist in both sources. It matters for the app because it changes whether these surface as Hayato-specific recommendations or as a shared Sengoku prompt. Note that the pre-v266 class doc treats Princess Sakuno's Blessing as a core Hayato skill throughout its rotation sections, which leans toward Grandis's reading, but that doc is pre-revamp and same-family with Grandis so it does not settle anything.

coverageGaps: HEXA investment order - no usable public source exists for the post-v266 class. Re-confirmed 2026-09-12 against all four reachable sources. Not blocking at Lv 236 (6th job unlocks at 260) but must be filled before endgame.

Hyper stat priority - no post-revamp source, and the one stale source explicitly declines to rank, telling readers to split points evenly. Direct users to MathBro's Hyper Stat Optimizer, which computes it per character.
Boost node tier order - a source exists but four separate reads produced four different orderings.
Active hyper skills are now NAMED (Bushido, Akatsuki Blessing, [Shinsoku] Silent Arc) but no source states a selection recommendation among them.
Independent confirmation for [Shinsoku] Crashing Tide and [Shinsoku] Light Cutter - both rest on DigitalTQ alone.
Per-level link skill values - only the max-level value is sourced.
No endgame claim in this file reaches 'strong' (3+ independent sources). The public Hayato record supports at most two independent post-revamp sources on any single point.
researchNotes: Hayato is structurally harder to source than most classes for a reason worth recording: it is a Japan-originated class, so the KMS cross-check lane that the project brief relies on for other classes (NamuWiki, Orange Mushroom) does not usefully exist. A search of Orange Mushroom returned no Hayato posts, and the NamuWiki Hayato pages returned HTTP 403 to fetching on both URL forms tried. maplestorywiki.net/w/Hayato/Skills - the intended anti-fabrication name-validation table - returned 403 to fetching and the browser was denied navigation to that host, and the Fandom mirror returned HTTP 402. Skill names in this file were therefore validated by triangulation across three separately authored sources instead of against a neutral wiki table; every skill name recorded here appears in at least two of those, except where explicitly marked single-source. The web search budget for this session was exhausted (200/200) before this class was researched, so all findings come from direct fetches of URLs already known from the project's discovery phase. Nexon's official v266 patch notes are JS-rendered and returned an empty shell; reading them in a browser would be the cleanest way to validate the post-revamp skill list independently and is the recommended next step, alongside a human pass on the Hayato Discord for HEXA order.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm.
contest.resolutionMethod: Each disputed claim was settled by reopening the exact cited page. Critically, the v252 class doc was pulled as its plain-text export (docs.google.com/document/d/<id>/export?format=txt) rather than through a summarising fetch - its recommendation tables are two-column layouts and its node priority table is a strip of images, both of which defeat naive extraction and produced contradictory readings on both sides of this dispute. Two of the five defects turned out to be extraction artifacts in the CRITIC's own reading and were refuted with verbatim text; two were upheld and fixed; one was upheld and recorded as a conflict.

resolved.defect: FALSE SOURCE CLAIM - vMatrix.trios[4] said the v252 class doc 'also put Princess Sakuno's Blessing in its high-priority list'; the critic reported it is in that doc's LOW priority list, making the file use a deprioritisation as corroboration.
resolved.verdict: CORRECTED - and the critic's counter-reading is also unsupported.
resolved.what: The doc's Node Priority section is a High-to-Low gradient rendered as images. In the plain-text export the cells are empty; all that survives is the axis words 'High', 'Boost Nodes', 'Low'. Neither 'high-priority list' nor 'LOW priority list' is readable - both were inferred from the same broken table. What IS readable is the doc's annotating prose, which says 'Princess Sakuno's Blessing provides a massive Final Damage Buff, ramping up as it persists. This FD ramps up faster the higher level it is and is vital to Hayato's burst.' That is an endorsement, not a deprioritisation. Nonetheless the doc was DROPPED as a source for this claim entirely, for reasons that hold regardless of which reading is right: it is pre-v266, and it shares the Hayato Discord upstream with Grandis Library, so it was never an independent second source. The entry is now single-source on DigitalTQ and labelled weak, down from moderate. The doc's endorsement is retained only as a flagged, explicitly non-confidence-raising historical note.

resolved.defect: FALSE SOURCE CLAIM - the same entry said the class doc 'independently echoed' the Twilight Bloom + Princess Sakuno's Blessing pair; 'Twilight Bloom' does not appear in that document.
resolved.what: Confirmed by case-insensitive grep of the doc's 74KB plain-text export: 'twilight' appears ZERO times. The 'independently echoed' clause has been removed outright. This was the load-bearing half of the old moderate label.

resolved.defect: MISATTRIBUTED CORROBORATION - innerAbility.bossing[2] said the class doc listed Weapon Attack 15-21 and Buff Duration 38% as non-top BOSSING lines; the critic reported 38% Buff Duration is in the doc's FARMING list, and that gearingNotes item 5 built an Akatsuki/buff-duration theory on the misreading.
resolved.verdict: REFUTED - the file's claim was correct and is CONFIRMED.
resolved.what: Verbatim from the plain-text export, the bossing column contains one either/or cell reading '15 - 21 Weapon Attack / or / 38% Buff Duration'. The farming column is fully and separately accounted for by its own three rows: '18 - 20% Meso Obtained or 18 - 20% Item Drop', '13 - 15% Meso Obtained ... or 13 - 15% Item Drop', '7 - 8% Damage Increase to Normal Monsters'. There is no spare farming slot for Buff Duration to occupy. The doc's own FAQ independently agrees: 'Does Hayato need Buff Duration? Yes, but at a lower priority to other stats.' The critic's reading came from the same flattened two-column table. gearingNotes item 5 is therefore left standing. What DID change: sourceCount dropped to 1 and consensus to weak, because Grandis and the doc are one consensus family.

resolved.defect: UNVERIFIED DETAIL - innerAbility.training[0] said the class doc 'gave 18-20% Meso Obtained and 18-20% Item Drop'; the critic found Meso Obtained only, with no Item Drop line, and flagged it for re-checking before shipping.
resolved.verdict: REFUTED - the file's claim was correct and is CONFIRMED.
resolved.what: Verbatim from the plain-text export: '18 - 20% Meso Obtained' / 'or' / '18 - 20% Item Drop'. The Item Drop half is present. The critic flagged this one as lower-confidence and suspected its own fetch summarisation might be lossy; it was. What DID change: sourceCount dropped to 1 and consensus to weak on the same one-consensus-family grounds.

resolved.defect: MISCHARACTERISED CLASS FACT - vMatrix.trios[4] labelled Twilight Bloom and Princess Sakuno's Blessing 'Cross-class Sengoku nodes ... not Hayato-specific', which is DigitalTQ's framing, while Grandis lists BOTH as Hayato's own 5th job skills - and that disagreement was nowhere in the conflicts array.
resolved.verdict: UPHELD - conflict RECORDED and the label CORRECTED.
resolved.what: Both readings re-verified verbatim. DigitalTQ: 'All Sengoku classes should try to also obtain these: Twilight Bloom, Princess Sakuno's Blessing.' Grandis lists both among Hayato's 5th job skills alongside Shogetsu Form, Weapon Aura, Impenetrable Skin and [Battou] Wailing Heavens. A fourth entry has been added to the conflicts array, and the trio entry's label now states both positions instead of asserting only DigitalTQ's.

additionalCorrectionsNotInDefects: hyperSkills.passives were labelled 'strong' on the strength of two independent sources. Strong requires 3+. All five downgraded to moderate. The claim itself is unchanged and remains the best-sourced judgement in the file.
hexa.skillNames.commonCore ('Sol Janus') was labelled 'strong' while citing a single page, justified by general game knowledge rather than a source count. Downgraded to weak.

All six innerAbility lines were labelled 'moderate' by counting Grandis Library and the v252 class doc as two sources. The file's own commonMistakes entry warns against exactly that - they share the Hayato Discord upstream. All six downgraded to weak, sourceCount 1, with the doc's agreement retained in a 'familyCorroboration' field explicitly marked independent:false.

hyperStats' stale claim rendered the doc's five-item bossing pool as a three-item 'focus' - silently dropping Damage and Critical Rate, and implying a ranking. Corrected to the full unordered set, restructured as 'staleUnorderedSet' with ordered:false, and annotated with the doc's own instruction to split hyper stat points evenly. hyperStats.priority stays empty.

hyperSkills.actives was empty. Bushido, Akatsuki Blessing and [Shinsoku] Silent Arc are each named as hyper skills by two independent sources and are now recorded - explicitly as a DESCRIPTIVE list, since no source states an active selection recommendation.

vMatrix gained a second priority entry for the four 5th job skill nodes DigitalTQ says to obtain (Shogetsu Form, Crashing Tide, Light Cutter, Wailing Heavens), flagged unordered. These were previously in the file only under a HEXA heading.

vMatrix.priority[0] was labelled 'moderate' partly on the grounds that one page had been read three times consistently. Repeat reads of one page are not independent sources; downgraded to weak, sourceCount 1.

Every array that could be misread as a ranking now carries an explicit unordered flag or note: vMatrix.priority entries, hexa mastery and enhancement core name lists, hyperSkills passives and actives, and the stale hyper stat set.
contest.outOfScopeNote: None of the five defects concerned jobs 1-4 skill builds, skill damage coefficients, damage lines, job tiers or rotations. All five landed in the endgame sections and all five were settled. skillBuilds and coefficient content in this file was not touched.
contest.shipReadyNote: Every claim in vMatrix, hexa, hyperSkills, hyperStats and innerAbility was re-opened against its cited page on 2026-09-12 and is either verified against verbatim source text or deleted. Nothing in those five sections reaches 'strong' consensus, and nothing claims to. The remaining gaps - HEXA order, boost node tier order, hyper stat ranking - are recorded as gaps with empty fields rather than as low-confidence guesses.
